resources.d: (Buncombe DSS): 40 Coxe Ave, 828-250-5500. State/federal vouchers, ages 0-12, for parents working or in school full-time; parents pay ~10% of gross monthly income. Also covers kinship and family-friend-neighbor care. 150+ participating programs. Expect waitlists; get on the list even mid-crisis. (The Dec 2025 federal funding freeze does NOT affect NC subsidies.) Per the Drive childcare guide: a decision is due within 30 days of a signed application; eligibility lasts 12 months; report a new job, address or household change within 5 working days; families with CPS, child welfare or foster care involvement pay no parent fee; and when income rises past the limit there is a 12-month phase-out instead of a cliff. A voucher can be used at any 4- or 5-star licensed program. Get on the list even while waiting, because some charities ask for proof of a pending application. Some centers charge the gap between the state rate and their price, so ask before enrolling. Monthly income limits for families with a child under 6 (Aug 2026 guide): 2 people $3,525, 3 $4,442, 4 $5,358, 5 $6,275.
resources.t: Kids / 0-5 | Verified 2 Aug 2026: the subsidy is WAITLISTED right now. Priority goes to children in protective services and children who are homeless, and those can enrol now. Apply anyway and apply immediately, because the waitlist is date-ordered and applying is what secures a priority slot when one opens. Family pays about 10% of gross monthly income.

resources.d: funds respite childcare for Buncombe kids birth-18 with disability, chronic condition, or significant behavioral/medical needs. AmyHobson@eckerd.org / amy.hobson@caring4children.org, 828-785-1590. How it works, per the guide: the parent picks the respite caregiver (18 or older and not living in the home, often someone the child already knows), pays them, sends a monthly timesheet by 9am on the last Monday, and is reimbursed by direct deposit. No work requirement. Apply with a W-9. 2026-27 application: scholarships run July 2026 to June 2027 for Buncombe and Henderson counties, for families of children with emotional, behavioral or medical needs or families facing risk factors. Send the application, a W-9 and the direct-deposit form with a voided check to the director. The money is for the caregiver to get a break: the application says it cannot pay for care during the parent's appointments, surgery or recovery, work, school or errands (that is child care), for camps or after-school programs, or for the parent's own outing costs. resources.d: 165 S French Broad Ave, 828-239-3531, haca.org. Public housing and Section 8 (online applications). The Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program provides case management that also unlocks a Working Wheels referral. Apply online through the RENTCafe applicant portal (haca.org, Apply for Housing; register without a code). No internet or need an accommodation: the Admissions Office at 165 S French Broad Ave takes walk-ins Tuesdays 9am-5pm, appointments Mon, Wed and Thu. Expect a wait of up to about three years; keep the address and phone current in the portal, because a missed waitlist purge letter removes the family. Local preferences include homelessness and fleeing domestic violence. The guide says a 15-hour-a-week work or school rule applies from 2026-27 for adults who are not 62+, disabled, or the main caregiver of a child under 6; confirm with HACA. Once housed, the Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program puts rent increases from new earnings into an escrow savings account.
resources.t: Verified 8/2026. HCV AND public housing waitlists both OPEN as of mid-2026, online only via RENTCafe. Walk-ins Tuesdays; M/W/Th by appointment. Waitlist status: Caroline Logan 828-239-3532. Porting in: 828-259-1222. All admissions preferences were removed in 2024, so position is date and time of application only. Apply same day.

resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: No-cost extras most families are never told about. School supplies up to $50 for ages 6 to 18, JUNE THROUGH SEPTEMBER ONLY. 24 hours of free virtual tutoring for eligible members ages 6 to 18. Up to $100 toward after-school sports and activities. GED exam voucher, $160 value. Chromebook for members ages 17 to 18 who recently graduated or finished a GED.
resources.h: Member Services 844-594-5070 (TTY 711), Mon-Sat 7am-6pm. Or redeem in the Benefit Reward Hub after logging in at healthybluenc.com.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on healthybluenc.com/medicaid/benefits. The school supply window CLOSES 30 SEPTEMBER, so this is a call to make now, not in October. Standard Plan Healthy Blue only. Children in foster care are usually on Healthy Blue Care Together, a separate plan with separate numbers.

resources.n: Healthy Blue extra benefits - food, a phone, hotel and housing help
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Three months of fresh fruit and vegetables, up to $120 value, or a $120 grocery card. A phone with unlimited talk and text and 10GB of data a month, more for those who qualify. Help with hotel costs after an inpatient hospital stay. Help with housing insecurity and pending homelessness. Up to 10 rides to personal, non-medical appointments for members using long-term services and supports. Uber gift card, plus rides to the doctor and the pharmacy.
resources.h: Member Services 844-594-5070 (TTY 711), Mon-Sat 7am-6pm, or the Benefit Reward Hub.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026. WARNING, the printed Sept 2025 handbook is now WRONG on the amounts: it says $20 rideshare gift card, up to $500 for a hotel, and up to $500 for moving expenses. The live site drops those dollar figures and has replaced moving expenses with housing insecurity help. Ask what the current amount is. Do not quote the handbook to a family. Eligibility rules apply to the food, hotel and housing items.

resources.n: Healthy Blue extra benefits - pregnancy and new baby
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Rewards up to $75 for going to prenatal and postpartum visits. A Baby Essentials catalog to choose from, including diapers, a safe sleep kit and a breastfeeding support kit. A community baby shower. Doula support in select counties. Healthy Blue also covers one postpartum home visit for newborn care within 60 days of delivery.
resources.h: Member Services 844-594-5070 (TTY 711), Mon-Sat 7am-6pm. Tell them you are pregnant as early as possible.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026. Doula support is listed as available in SELECT counties. Confirm Buncombe before promising it to anyone. Vaya Total Care does this differently: a free breast pump through Aeroflow plus Lactation Link support, usable within 365 days of the first prenatal visit, if that visit happened inside the first 16 weeks. Aeroflow 1-844-867-9890.

resources.n: Healthy Blue extra benefits - sensory, asthma, exercise, pain, med lockbox
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Sensory toys up to $100 value. Asthma and allergy relief kit for adults and children. Choice of 2 items from an exercise catalog OR $75 toward a gym membership. WW (WeightWatchers) voucher, 13 weeks. Up to 6 acupuncture treatments. Up to 5 extra chiropractor visits. A medicine safety kit with a lockbox and pill case. Pain products up to $25. Scale and blood pressure cuff.
resources.h: Member Services 844-594-5070 (TTY 711), Mon-Sat 7am-6pm, or the Benefit Reward Hub.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026. The $100 sensory allowance and the free medicine lockbox are the two most useful here for a family with a neurodivergent child. Sensory items sit under long-term services and supports, so eligibility may be narrower than the marketing suggests. Ask directly rather than assuming a no.

resources.n: Healthy Blue Care Together - different plan, different numbers, caregiver therapy
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: The statewide specialty plan for children and youth in foster care, receiving adoption assistance, or otherwise involved with child welfare, and for former foster youth. It carries benefits the Standard Plan does not have: THERAPY FOR CAREGIVERS, up to 12 sessions a year; up to $100 toward a youth club membership; monthly money toward food, childcare or transportation; school supply stipends; luggage and clothing; prenatal doula; wellness rewards; care management; in lieu of services.
resources.h: Member Services 833-777-3611, 7am-6pm including state holidays. Crisis line 833-597-3985, 24/7. TTY 711.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on healthybluenc.com. Do NOT call the regular Healthy Blue numbers for these families. Caregiver therapy at 12 sessions a year is the standout: it funds the ADULT’S own therapy, not the child’s, which is the two-generation piece that usually has no funding attached. Confirm which plan a child is actually on through the Enrollment Broker, 1-833-870-5500, before you start dialling.

resources.n: Free nurse line at 3am - both Medicaid plans
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: A free 24/7 call to a registered nurse. Should I take them to the ER. Is this fever an emergency. Is this rash something. What happens if I missed a dose. No cost, no appointment, no waiting for the office to open. Healthy Blue 24/7 NurseLine 844-545-1427 (TTY 711). Vaya Nurse Line 1-800-290-1623.
resources.h: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, both plans.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on both plan websites. This is the direct answer to the 2am problem. The alternative at 2am is a long ER wait with a child who is already dysregulated, and a bill. Worth writing on the fridge alongside 988.

resources.n: EPSDT - the rule that overturns a "no" for anyone under 21
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: For any Medicaid member under 21, a plan CANNOT say no just because a service is not in its coverage policy or goes past a policy limit. It has to run a separate EPSDT review and approve the service if it would correct or improve the condition, keep it from getting worse, or prevent another condition. Under 21 there are also no copays, no limit on how often a service is given, no limit on how many services in one day, and services can be delivered where the child actually is, including school and community settings.
resources.h: The PROVIDER has to make the request and has to explain in writing how the service will help. Ask them to use the words "EPSDT review" in the request.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified in both the Vaya and Healthy Blue member handbooks. This is the strongest single lever in this guide: therapy hours, ABA, equipment, private duty nursing, anything the plan calls over the limit. If they still deny after an EPSDT review, the clock is 60 days to appeal, 30 days for a decision, 72 hours if expedited.

resources.n: When the plan denies something - the clock, and the free help
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: 60 days from the date on the denial letter to file an appeal. The plan then has 30 days to decide. Ask for an EXPEDITED appeal and it drops to 72 hours if waiting would harm health, and the provider can request it too. If a service the child ALREADY HAS is being cut or stopped, ask for continuation of benefits within 10 days of the notice and it keeps running until the appeal is decided. If the appeal is lost, 120 days to ask for a State Fair Hearing. The Mediation Network calls within 5 business days to offer a free, optional mediation before the hearing.
resources.h: NC Medicaid Ombudsman 877-201-3750, free and independent of the plan. Mediation Network of NC 336-461-3300. Office of Administrative Hearings 984-236-1860.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified in both handbooks. TWO CAUTIONS. First, the NC Medicaid Ombudsman is NOT the Long-Term Care Ombudsman at Land of Sky: different program, different job. Second, if a family asks for continuation of benefits and then LOSES the appeal, the plan is allowed to bill them for what it paid during the appeal, though only with NC Medicaid approval first. Say that out loud before a family chooses it.

resources.n: Why Medicaid rides get suspended - the rules nobody explains
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Book at least 2 business days ahead. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead or it can count as a no-show. Healthy Blue: 3 or more missed trips in 3 months can suspend rides for up to 30 days. Vaya: more than 2 missed trips in 3 months, same. Good cause covers your own illness, or the illness or death of a spouse, child or parent. Even while suspended, rides to dialysis and chemotherapy continue. Vaya must give a suspended member who cannot pay a gas voucher or mileage reimbursement IN ADVANCE for Medicaid-covered trips. Rides also cover an attendant, and a parent or guardian travelling with a child member.
resources.h: Vaya via Modivcare 1-888-621-2084. Healthy Blue via Modivcare 855-397-3602. NC Medicaid Direct via Land of Sky 828-552-5486. Urgent trips can be booked 24/7: sick visits, hospital discharge, life-sustaining treatment.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026. CORRECTION: this guide previously listed 855-397-3604 for Healthy Blue in 10 places. That is Modivcare’s provider network line, not the member line. Corrected to 855-397-3602 on 4 Aug 2026. Vaya will also consider a trip so BOTH parents can accompany a child, and a trip so a parent can be taught to care for a child who is inpatient. Both need prior approval, so ask early.

resources.n: Free interpreter, ASL, Braille and large print from the health plan
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Both plans must provide, free of charge: a qualified interpreter in any language, spoken or written; qualified ASL interpreters; certified deaf interpreters; CART captioning; assistive listening devices; large print, Braille, audio and accessible electronic formats; speech-to-speech relay. They will also tell you whether a specific doctor’s office is wheelchair accessible and help make or get to the appointment.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified in both handbooks. If a provider tells a family to bring their own interpreter, that is the plan’s problem to fix, not the family’s. Call Member Services and file it as a grievance: the plan must confirm receipt in 5 days and answer in writing within 30.

resources.n: Quit For Life - free coaching and free nicotine patches (Vaya)
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Vaya members get the Quit For Life program: free quit coaching, group video sessions, a digital dashboard, and FREE nicotine replacement such as patches or gum. Members who are pregnant or have behavioral health needs get extra support from dedicated coaching teams.
resources.h: Ask Vaya Member and Recipient Services, 1-800-962-9003, Mon-Sat 7am-6pm.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified in the Vaya handbook. The free nicotine replacement is the part almost nobody knows about. Healthy Blue covers smoking cessation agents including over-the-counter products through the pharmacy benefit, so ask there instead if the family is on the Standard Plan.

resources.n: 1915(i) services - Medicaid respite without waiting out Innovations
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: The services that replaced (b)(3) on 1 July 2023. Five of them: RESPITE, Community Living and Support, Individual and Transitional Support, Community Transition, and Supported Employment. The thing that makes this reachable is that 1915(i) does NOT require an institutional level of care, which Innovations does. Qualifying conditions are a serious mental health condition, a severe substance use disorder, an I/DD, or a TBI. Sitting on the Innovations Registry of Unmet Needs does not disqualify anyone, and using 1915(i) does NOT cost a family its place in that line. Being found eligible for 1915(i) also makes you eligible for Tailored Care Management. Call Vaya 1-800-962-9003 and ask the Tailored Care Manager for a 1915(i) independent assessment. It goes to the state; if eligible, the care manager writes the service into the care plan and submits it for prior authorisation. For children with severe medical needs or technology dependence, the CAP/C waiver counts only the child's income, not the parents'.
resources.t: Respite, Medicaid, Vaya, I/DD, Mental health, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on medicaid.ncdhhs.gov, page last modified 8 Jan 2026. Say "1915(i)", NOT "(b)(3)": the old name was retired and asking for it now can produce a false no. NOT available on Standard Plans (Healthy Blue, WellCare, UnitedHealthcare, AmeriHealth Caritas, Carolina Complete), so a Standard Plan family with a qualifying condition may need to ask the Enrollment Broker to move to the Tailored Plan first. Anyone who ALREADY holds an Innovations or TBI Waiver slot is not eligible, because those waivers already cover it. This is the widest respite door in this file for a child with a mental health diagnosis and no I/DD.
resources.src: WNC_Family_Resources_SNIFF_v19_Aug2026.xlsx, ALL RESOURCES tab; Drive: Free Childcare Leicester NC (14 Aug 2026)

resources.n: In Lieu of Services - the alternatives to residential, PRTF and the ER
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Vaya-approved substitutes for standard Medicaid services. Each one is a step DOWN from a placement or an ER trip, and families are almost never told they exist. For children and youth: HIGH-FIDELITY WRAPAROUND (in place of residential level II), FAMILY-CENTERED TREATMENT delivered in the home (in place of a level III group home), CHILD ACT (in place of a PRTF), ENHANCED CRISIS RESPONSE (for a youth at risk of the ER, or already in one and unable to go home), IN-HOME THERAPY (in place of intensive in-home or MST), OUTPATIENT PLUS (when plain outpatient is not enough), RAPID CARE (up to 24 hours in a facility instead of the ER or an admission), and TRANSITIONAL YOUTH SERVICES for ages 16 to 21 (in place of residential). For adults: long-term community supports, dual-diagnosis ACT, first-episode psychosis ACT, and a crisis risk assessment at a behavioural health urgent care instead of the ER. Ask the provider or care manager to request the service BY NAME. A family can also call Vaya 1-800-962-9003 and ask which of these are contracted near them.
resources.t: Vaya, Medicaid, Crisis, Mental health, Kids / 0-5, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, from the Vaya member handbook v3.0 (20 Nov 2025) cross-checked against the live ILOS policy page. A family has the RIGHT to refuse an in lieu of service and demand the original service instead, and the right to appeal. Vaya cannot cut or remove one mid-year without NC Medicaid approval and 30 days written notice. The list does change: the live page also shows Critical Time Intervention and ACT Step Down, which are not in the handbook, so confirm the specific one before promising it.

resources.n: Free meals delivered after a hospital stay (Mom's Meals)
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Two home-delivered meals a day for up to seven days, so 14 meals, in the month after discharge from a qualifying inpatient hospital stay. A psychiatric admission counts. No cost. Delivered by Mom's Meals. Ask the care manager BEFORE a planned admission, during the stay, or straight after discharge. The window closes 30 days after the discharge date.
resources.t: Food, Medicaid, Vaya, Mobile / delivery, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on vayahealth.com. THE HANDBOOK OMITS TWO CONDITIONS that will get a family denied: you must be participating in Tailored Care Management, and you must not already be eligible for meal delivery through the Innovations Waiver. Also, an ER visit and an outpatient surgery performed at a hospital do NOT count as a qualifying stay. The Nov 2025 handbook says only "fourteen meals" and "within one month". Best use here is a parent coming home after a psychiatric admission or a birth, into a house with no groceries.

resources.n: Vaya pays for the GED, exam fees included (GEDWorks)
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: A voucher covering a one-to-one BILINGUAL advisor, study materials in English or Spanish, GED-Ready practice tests AND the GED tests themselves, expert tutors, a private online student support group, and college-ready credits. Test-pass guarantee: unlimited access to the programme until the student passes. The voucher does not depend on exam results. Start at ged.com/vaya-health/. Eligibility is confirmed online, then GEDWorks takes over directly. Must be 18 or over, a Vaya Total Care Medicaid member, and not already hold a high school equivalency.
resources.t: Free, Vaya, Medicaid, Spanish / bilingual, Adult education | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on vayahealth.com. The exam fee is the wall most people hit, and this pays it. Standard Plan equivalent: Healthy Blue reimburses up to $80 toward GED test fees, which is less. Two-generation: a parent finishing a GED moves the household income ceiling, not just their own resume. Also on the Vaya perks list and not given its own row here: a six-month WeightWatchers app voucher, for members 18+ with a BMI of 25 or higher, one per calendar year, requested through the Member and Recipient Portal with medical documentation.

resources.n: $10 for a flu or COVID shot, $25 for a well-child visit
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: A $10 gift card, choice of Amazon, Target or Walmart, for each COVID-19 or flu vaccine, up to two per plan year. This one is open to ALL AGES, so a child's shot counts. Separately, a $25 gift card for attending a yearly physical or wellness visit, but only for NC Innovations Waiver participants under 18. Submit the request plus proof of the vaccine or the visit through the Member and Recipient Portal at memberportal.vayahealth.com. Allow up to 30 days for approval.
resources.t: Medicaid, Vaya, Kids / 0-5, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on vayahealth.com. The $25 wellness-visit card is NOT in the Nov 2025 handbook at all, only on the live site, so nobody working from the PDF knows it exists. Small money, but it is money for something the family is already being asked to do, and it is one of the few perks that reaches a child directly. Requires portal access: worth setting the account up with a family during a visit rather than leaving it as homework.

resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: A $100 discount toward home safety and assistance equipment that Medicaid will NOT pay for as durable medical equipment: door and motion sensors that prompt or alert, environmental controls for someone with limited mobility, electronic medication dispensers, personal emergency devices, and video monitoring. Through the care manager, who checks eligibility and books a consultation with Simply Home to match products to the person.
resources.t: Autism, I/DD, Medicaid, Vaya, Safety, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on vayahealth.com. Four conditions: Vaya Total Care Medicaid, participating in Tailored Care Management, an I/DD diagnosis, and receiving independent living services. You do NOT need an Innovations slot or a spot on the waitlist. For a family whose child elopes or wanders at night, the door and motion sensor category is the thing to ask about first, and it is the category DME reliably refuses.

resources.n: How fast the plan is REQUIRED to get you seen
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: These are contractual maximum waits, not suggestions. MOBILE CRISIS: 2 HOURS. Mental health or substance use URGENT: 24 hours. Mental health ROUTINE: 14 days. Substance use ROUTINE: 48 HOURS. Well-child visit: 14 days if the child is under 6 months, 30 days if older. Adult preventive: 30 days. First prenatal visit: 14 days in the 1st or 2nd trimester, 5 DAYS in the 3rd trimester or a high-risk pregnancy. If a family is quoted a longer wait, call Vaya Member and Recipient Services 1-800-962-9003 and say the standard out loud. If nothing moves, file it as a grievance.
resources.t: Medicaid, Vaya, Advocacy, Mental health, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, from the Appointment Guide in the Vaya member handbook v3.0. The 48-hour substance use standard is the one nobody uses and it is the strongest thing on this list: a parent who says yes on a Friday should not be told to call back in three weeks. A grievance must be acknowledged in writing within 5 days and answered within 30. This is a number to hand the family so THEY can say it, not only something the FRP says on their behalf.

resources.n: Keeping the provider you already trust when the plan changes
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: On joining Vaya you can keep an OUT-OF-NETWORK provider for UP TO 180 DAYS if you are mid-course of treatment or have an ongoing condition, and the handbook names I/DD, a mental health diagnosis, substance use disorder and TBI as qualifying. More than 3 months pregnant: keep the provider through delivery plus 60 days postpartum. Pregnant and seeing a behavioural health provider: through delivery. A scheduled surgery or inpatient stay: through the procedure plus 90 days of follow-up. Terminally ill: for the rest of your life. Separately, a SECOND OPINION needs no prior authorisation, in network or out. Tell the care manager you want to keep the provider. They document it and start an Out-of-Network Agreement, roughly 3 business days. Or call 1-800-962-9003.
resources.t: Medicaid, Vaya, Advocacy, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, from the Vaya member handbook v3.0. This matters right now: Vaya and Partners become VAYA PARTNERS on 1 October 2026 and networks will be redrawn. Any family mid-treatment should have this sentence ready before then. If a PCP leaves the network Vaya must tell the family in writing within 7 days, 15 days for any other provider. Continuity is a right here, not a favour, and a child should not have to restart a therapeutic relationship because the state redrew a map.

resources.n: Never leave the pharmacy without the medicine
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Copays are capped at $4 a prescription, and there is NO copay at all for anyone under 21, for pregnancy-related care, for behavioural health, I/DD or TBI services, for Innovations participants, or for children in foster care. If a family cannot pay the $4 that day, the pharmacy CAN hand over the medicine and bill later, and a provider cannot refuse care over an unpaid copay. If a prescription needs prior authorisation, the pharmacy can dispense a 72-HOUR SUPPLY while it is decided, and the decision is due within 24 hours. Vaya Pharmacy Service Line 1-800-540-6083, Mon to Sat 7am to 6pm. Preferred Drug List at vayahealth.com/benefits-services/pharmacy/medication-search/.
resources.t: Medicaid, Vaya, Pharmacy, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, from the Vaya member handbook v3.0. The 72-hour bridge supply is the sentence to say out loud at the counter, and almost nobody does. Out-of-network pharmacy: the family may have to pay full price, then claim it back with the manual claim form on vayahealth.com. A child leaving hospital on a Friday with an unfilled prior authorisation is the exact case this solves.

resources.n: Advance Instruction for Mental Health Treatment - deciding now, for later
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: A free legal document saying which mental health treatments you do and do not want, and who speaks for you, if there is ever a point where you cannot speak for yourself. It can also nominate a guardian in advance. It can stand alone or be combined with a health care power of attorney. It only takes effect once a doctor or eligible psychologist states in writing that you cannot make or communicate the decision, and you can change or revoke it at any time. Free forms at sosnc.gov/ahcdr. Registering with the NC Secretary of State makes it findable by a hospital at 2am. Vaya will help a member understand or obtain the documents: 1-800-962-9003.
resources.t: Free, Mental health, Legal, Advocacy | Added 4 Aug 2026, from the Vaya member handbook v3.0. For a parent with a history of involuntary commitment, this is the most control-restoring piece of paper available and it costs nothing. NUMBER CONFLICT: the handbook prints 1-919-807-2167 in the text and 1-919-814-5400 in its own phone list, two pages apart. Try 807-2167 first. NC also recognises living wills and health care powers of attorney, same registry.

resources.n: What a young person can consent to on their own
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Under NC law a minor can consent, without a parent or guardian, to four things: treatment for sexually transmitted infections, services related to pregnancy, help with alcohol or other substance use, and help with emotional conditions. On top of that, no referral is needed for a first behavioural health or substance use assessment in any 12-month period, and none is ever needed for mobile crisis. Any Vaya network provider. Behavioural Health Crisis Line 1-800-849-6127, 24/7, any age. 988 also takes calls and texts at any age.
resources.t: Teens, Mental health, Medicaid, Vaya, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, from the member rights section of the Vaya member handbook v3.0. Worth saying plainly to a 15-year-old and to the adult in the room at the same time: this is written into the plan, not a loophole. It does not remove the parent, it removes the wait. Useful when a teenager will talk to somebody but not yet to their family.

resources.n: My Village Asheville - voluntary child hosting, parent keeps custody
resources.spd: Not stated in the source. Ask when you call. Their materials are English-only online.
resources.d: Church-based volunteer host families care for your children short term while you deal with a crisis. THE PARENT NEVER LOSES CUSTODY and can ask for the children home whenever they want. Contact stays open the whole time: visits, texts, FaceTime, phone calls. Average hosting is 4 to 6 weeks, range is one day to a year. Reasons families use it, in their own words: medical emergency, homelessness, an expected baby, a treatment or recovery programme, mental health care, and gaps between employment and childcare. Free. A Community Coach also works with the PARENT on the parent's own goals, and visits the host home within the first two days. Referral line 828-357-7075, Mon-Fri 9am-5pm. THIS IS NOT A 24/7 CRISIS LINE. As an FRP use the agency referral form at myvillageasheville.org/referrals, and call the line too, which is what they ask agency workers to do. Families can self-refer at myvillageasheville.org/support.
resources.t: Respite, Host home, Free, Faith-based, Voluntary, Pregnancy, Kids / 0-5 | Added 17 Aug 2026, verified on myvillageasheville.org. SAY THIS TO THE FAMILY BEFORE YOU REFER: it is an explicitly Christian organisation working through local churches. They say themselves that a family's views do not need to match theirs to use the service, but a family deserves to know before they walk in, not after. Host families are volunteers, screened by application, home evaluation and safety checklist, fingerprinting and background checks, character references, interview and training. They are NOT DSS-licensed foster homes, and this is NOT a licensed placement. Because it is private and voluntary there is no DSS oversight and no Medicaid appeal route if something goes wrong. IT DOES NOT REPLACE A REPORT: if a safety concern meets the reporting threshold, report it. This was Alongside Families Asheville until 7 JULY 2025, when My Village Ministries took the site over with no programme change and no volunteer retraining. Sister chapter Elizabeth's House at My Village, Hickory, Catawba County, referral line 828-330-3494, runs the same model with a focus on pregnant and single mothers: only relevant if a family has ties out that way.

resources.note: The Drive respite guide (Aug 2026) says My Village Asheville used to be called Alongside Families. The Public Edition (Nov 2026) lists Alongside Families (alongsidefamilies.org) separately, as home visiting for immigrant and refugee families. Check which is current before referring.

resources.n: Free monthly dads' group: early childhood and relationship-led parenting
resources.spd: Not stated in the source. Ask when you call.
resources.d: An intentional space for dads to build community around early childhood development and attachment, and to move from reactive to relationship-led parenting. Free, meets monthly; the next meeting was posted for 11 November 2026.
resources.src: Facebook post in Asheville Natural Mamas & Papas, 16 Oct 2026 (Facebook deep scrape part 3, 6 Nov 2026)
resources.note: The post does not name the host or the place. Message the poster through the link to ask where it meets.

resources.n: Play Talk & Grow - speech, feeding, AAC, takes Medicaid and Vaya
resources.d: Pediatric speech and language, birth to 18, in the clinic and inside some daycares and private schools. Not just articulation. They do AAC (talkers and communication boards), LAMP motor planning, Natural Language Acquisition for gestalt language processors and children who talk in scripts or echolalia, SPELLING TO COMMUNICATE for minimally speaking or unreliably speaking autistic kids, PROMPT for childhood apraxia, DIRFloortime, feeding and swallowing therapy (chewing, safe swallowing, expanding what a child will eat), literacy and dyslexia work, and stuttering. Parents sit IN the session and get coached, which is the part that makes it carry over at home. resources.t: Autism, School, ESA+, Opportunity Scholarship, Private school, Deadline | Added 17 Aug 2026, verified on campfireaba.info. FOUR THINGS A FAMILY MUST KNOW BEFORE THEY MOVE A CHILD. (1) THE OPPORTUNITY SCHOLARSHIP WINDOW FOR 2026-27 CLOSED AT 5PM ON 14 AUGUST 2026, four days before this row was written, so a family reading 'apply for Opportunity/ESA+' on the school's page today has already missed that one for this year. ESA+ has its own timeline: check k12.ncseaa.edu, do not assume. (2) ESA+ REQUIRES AN ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION FROM A NORTH CAROLINA PUBLIC SCHOOL ISSUED IN THE LAST THREE YEARS. So the free school evaluation on the IX tab is not an alternative to this money, it is the DOOR to it: request it in writing from Buncombe County Schools EC and the clock starts. Awards run roughly $9,000 to $17,000. (3) ASK WHETHER THEY ARE A DIRECT PAYMENT SCHOOL OR A REIMBURSEMENT SCHOOL. A reimbursement school means the FAMILY PAYS TUITION UP FRONT and claims it back. No Child First family can front a year of private school tuition. Also confirm they are registered with DNPE and with NCSEAA, because a brand new school may not be yet, and without both the money cannot follow the child. (4) MOVING TO A PRIVATE SCHOOL GIVES UP THE IEP. Under IDEA the individual entitlement to a free appropriate public education belongs to children enrolled in public school. A privately enrolled child may get a services plan, which is a much weaker thing, decided by the district and shared out across all private-school children. This is the trade-off nobody mentions in the brochure and it is not reversible mid-year. It may still be the right call for a child who is suffering in their classroom. It is the family's call, made with the facts.
